disclosures.text: A suction chuck for attracting and holding a thin flat workpiece in a non-contact state.
A flat plate-shaped body with a compressed gas flow path formed inside.
A facing surface on the side of the body facing the workpiece.
The facing surface has multiple recesses as suction elements that generate negative pressure by ejecting compressed gas.
The facing surface is configured to completely encompass the shape of the workpiece when viewed perpendicularly.
The facing surface is similar in shape to the workpiece or offset outward from the workpiece shape.
All recesses are arranged to be encompassed within the shape of the workpiece when viewed perpendicularly.
A workpiece transfer device comprising the suction chuck and a compressed gas source.
The amount of compressed gas ejected from recesses in the center of the facing surface is greater than from recesses at the ends.
The device separates the top workpiece from a stacked bundle and holds it with the suction chuck.
Compressed gas is supplied to recesses at the ends of the facing surface first.
Then, compressed gas is supplied to recesses in the center of the facing surface.
This sequence holds the top workpiece of the bundle.

A suction chuck for holding a thin flat workpiece, comprising a flat body with internal compressed gas flow paths, and a facing surface with multiple recesses for generating negative pressure, where the facing surface encompasses the workpi
The facing surface and workpiece shape are right-angled quadrilaterals when viewed perpendicularly.
Exhaust holes are opened in the facing surface around the recesses to exhaust compressed gas.
All exhaust holes are arranged to be encompassed within the workpiece shape when viewed perpendicularly.
Multiple recesses are arranged in alignment parallel to the sides of the facing surface when viewed perpendicularly.
The recesses are cylindrical.
The body includes ejection flow paths that eject compressed gas along the inner wall of the recesses.
The ejection flow paths are formed parallel to the facing surface.
Multiple ejection flow paths are formed for one recess.
The body is formed by joining multiple plates in the thickness direction.
The plates include a first plate with the facing surface and a second plate connected to a compressed gas source.
The first plate has opening holes forming at least part of the recesses, opening to the facing surface.
The ejection flow paths are located between the facing surface and the second plate.
The second plate has a connection port for the compressed gas source on the side opposite the first plate.
The second plate has supply grooves on the first plate-facing side, forming supply flow paths to guide compressed gas to the ejection flow paths.
An intermediate plate is placed between the first and second plates.
The intermediate plate has slits forming the ejection flow paths, penetrating in the thickness direction.
A third plate is placed between the first and second plates.
The third plate has connection holes to connect the ejection flow paths and the supply grooves.
One side of the third plate in the thickness direction forms part of the inner wall of the ejection flow path.
The other side of the third plate in the thickness direction closes the open side of the supply groove, forming the supply flow path.
At least one supply flow path is connected to multiple ejection flow paths.
Multiple supply flow paths are provided.
Combinations of connection ports and ejection flow paths connected by each supply flow path are independent.
All multiple plates are made of metal.
The body is formed by diffusion bonding all stacked plates.
The multiple plates are made of stainless steel, aluminum alloy, or titanium alloy.
All multiple plates are made of the same metal material.
At least one of the recesses or ejection flow paths is formed by etching.
At least one of the recesses or ejection flow paths is formed by machining.
At least one of the connection ports or supply grooves is formed by machining.
A blowing device is provided to blow compressed gas towards the side surface of the workpiece bundle.
A parallel mechanism is provided to move the workpiece held by the suction chuck.
A SCARA arm is provided to move the workpiece held by the suction chuck.
The suction chuck is a Bernoulli chuck.
The workpiece is a solar cell wafer, fuel cell, secondary battery electrode, or separator.
The suction chuck is lightweight.
The suction chuck prevents workpiece damage from contact with the chuck edge during suction or release.
The facing surface is a rectangular flat surface.
The facing surface is a square flat surface.
The body is a plate laminate.
The plate laminate comprises a surface plate, a nozzle plate, a connection plate, and a distribution plate.
The surface plate has circular holes for ejecting swirling flow.
The nozzle plate has circular holes, elongated linear slits, and circular inflow holes.
Two slits and inflow holes are provided for each circular hole in the nozzle plate.
The connection plate has small circular connection holes.
The distribution plate has multiple circular connection ports and distribution grooves.
The compressed gas source can be a liquefied nitrogen tank.
The recesses are formed by the circular holes of the surface plate and nozzle plate, closed by the connection plate.
The distribution flow path is formed by the distribution groove closed by the connection plate.
The nozzle flow path is formed by the slit in the nozzle plate, closed by the surface plate and connection plate.
The nozzle flow path is parallel to the facing surface.
The exhaust holes allow air ejected from the recesses to escape upwards.
The plates are made of stainless steel.
The recesses are arranged in a 2x4 grid on the facing surface.
The exhaust holes are located between adjacent recesses in the vertical direction.
Each recess has two nozzle flow paths connected tangentially to its inner wall.
The two nozzle flow paths for one recess are 180 degrees out of phase.
Adjacent recesses have nozzle flow paths that create opposite swirling directions.
The suction chuck has 8 distribution flow paths, each corresponding to a 2x4 divided area of the facing surface.
Each distribution flow path connects one connection port and 8 recesses.
Compressed air is supplied to connection ports at one end of the facing surface first, then to central connection ports.
The timing of compressed air supply is controlled by electromagnetic valves.
The workpiece is held by peeling it up from the end.
Compressed air is supplied sequentially from one end recess, to central recesses, then to the other end recesses.
Compressed air is supplied sequentially from one corner recess to the other three corners.
Compressed air is supplied simultaneously to recesses at both ends, then to central recesses.
Multiple guide members are fixed to the edge of the body, spaced apart.
Two guide members are placed on each side of the rectangular body.
The guide members are perpendicular to the flat body.
The lower ends of the guide members protrude below the facing surface.
The guide members regulate relative movement of the workpiece parallel to the facing surface.
The workpiece supply device includes a support base, a lifting stage, a linear actuator, and an air nozzle.
The lifting stage supports a cassette containing stacked workpieces.
The air nozzle has a hollow cylindrical body with multiple blow-out holes.
The blow-out holes are arranged in a line at equal intervals along the cylinder axis.
The air nozzle body is positioned at approximately the same height as the cassette.
The air nozzle body is supported to be rotatable around its axis.
The air nozzle blows air to the side of the workpiece bundle.
The air blowing from the air nozzle is used in conjunction with time-lagged suction.
The suction chuck is mounted on a parallel mechanism robot.
The suction chuck is mounted on a SCARA arm robot.
The transfer robot can randomly access workpieces in a cassette by inserting the SCARA arm.
